sentences.text:
Mr. M.A. Khan, Assistant Government Advocate with
 Mr. Vipul Painuli, Brief Holder for the State of
 Uttarakhand.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)

The challenge in this petition is made to FIR/Case Crime No.529 of 2023, dated 20.09.2023, under
Sections 5(j)(i) of The Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and Sections 376(3),
506 Ipc, Police Station Patel Nagar, District Dehradun.

2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
3.
According to the FIR, on 14.05.2023, the petitioner forcibly raped the victim, a young girl of 14 years, who was then studying in Class VIIIth.
The victim could reveal the incident on 20.09.2023, to her parents when her health deteriorated.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the petitioner and victim, both are minors;
they are first cousin; the FIR is delayed.
5. This is writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.
If FIR discloses commission of offences, generally no interference is warranted unless there are compelling circumstances to do so.
6. According to the FIR, the petitioner is the cousin of the victim.
He forcibly raped her.
It is true that the FIR is little delayed, but what would be its effect, it will fall for scrutiny during the investigation or trial, as the case may be.
The FIR records that the victim was threatened by the petitioner.
It is only when the victim's health deteriorated then she could reveal the incident to her parents.

8. Having considered, this Court is of the view that there is no reason to make any interference in the matter.
Accordingly, the petition deserves to be dismissed at the stage of admission itself.
9. The petition is dismissed in limine.
(Ravindra Maithani, J.) 18.10.2023
